target.title: feat(config): add ordered config layers
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Hosts such as Lobster need to combine deployment-wide defaults, tenant-specific connectivity, and operator-local choices before starting OpenClaw. Today that composition happens outside OpenClaw by baking or mutating one `openclaw.json`, so OpenClaw cannot validate the original documents or enforce the authority boundary that produced the effective config.

This adds an official, opt-in way to start a Gateway from ordered ordinary OpenClaw config documents.

## Why core support instead of `$include` or launcher-side merging

`$include` is useful for assembling one authored config document. It does not express that an earlier source owns a value, reject a later source that tries to replace it, prove that later tool policy only tightens the effective policy, or make the resulting runtime immutable.

A launcher can implement those rules itself, but then it must duplicate OpenClaw's JSON5/include/env/schema/plugin validation and OpenClaw sees only the flattened result. That is the baked-overlay problem this PR is intended to remove.

The core addition is deliberately narrow: one repeatable CLI option, one recursive composer, and one startup-only/read-only lifecycle. It adds no config keys and no host-, tenant-, or operator-specific roles.

## User impact

No behavior changes unless `--config-layer` is supplied. Regular config users do not encounter this feature.

Opted-in Gateways use the composed snapshot for their lifetime. Config-mutating RPCs and persistence paths targeting that Gateway's canonical config are rejected, and config hot reload is disabled. Writes for unrelated config paths remain allowed. Restart with new source documents to activate a change.

## Example

Lobster can materialize three normal OpenClaw config files:

```json5
// scout-global.json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local" },
  tools: { deny: ["exec"] },
}
```

```json5
// tenant-network.json5
{
  gateway: {
    controlUi: {
      allowedOrigins: ["https://scout.example.tenant"],
    },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec", "web"] },
}
```

```json5
// operator-local.json5
{
  logging: { level: "debug" },
}
```

Then start OpenClaw explicitly:

```bash
openclaw gateway run \
  --config-layer global=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator-local.json5
```

The labels could be `one`, `two`, and `three`; only declaration order matters.

## Delivered V1

- repeat `--config-layer <id=path>` in precedence order
- parse through OpenClaw JSON5, include, env, schema, and plugin validation
- compose sparse documents recursively
- keep earlier exact values authoritative
- allow later `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` values only when they provably tighten policy
- keep the composed runtime startup-only and read-only
- scope persistence blocking to the layered Gateway's canonical config path
- treat pathless mutation preflights as targeting that canonical path, preventing plugin side effects before persistence

Layer IDs are descriptive only. Core has no built-in host, tenant, or operator roles.

## Evidence

Current reviewed head: `8dc592014ba01185adfa863b809702c62c3339c3`, rebased onto `578163c4a337fa7788252b1911d21680c2f6ccc9`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-layers.test.ts src/config/nix-mode-write-guard.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/config-layers.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts`
- 63 focused tests pass
- mixed-owner regression proves a layered path does not block an unrelated config path
- pathless-preflight regression proves early plugin/doctor/update guards resolve to the canonical owned path
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes
- final `codex review --base upstream/main`: no discrete actionable regression
- broader OpenClaw/Lobster prototype established the lifecycle constraints; this PR is the reduced startup-only slice
- Lobster fork adapter materializes the three files and launches OpenClaw with the repeated generic flags

Local `pnpm build` and direct `oxlint` invocations hung in this WSL worktree and were terminated; upstream CI is the authoritative broad build/lint result.

## Real behavior proof

The original foreground lifecycle proof established:

- Gateway logged `ready`; `GET /healthz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`
- `config.get` returned the tenant origin, `tools.deny: ["exec", "web"]`, and operator `logging.level: "info"`
- `config.patch` rejected with `configuration writes are unavailable while --config-layer is active`
- a fourth layer replacing tenant `allowedOrigins` rejected with `ControlledByEarlierLayer`
- the canonical config path remained absent

After the ownership fix and rebase, two additional real Gateway lanes ran on the exact current head:

- fresh state: startup and health passed, layered values were effective, canonical `openclaw.json` remained absent
- existing state: startup and health passed, layered values were effective, and the pre-existing canonical file's SHA-256 and legacy `meta.lastTouchedVersion` marker remained byte-for-byte unchanged

Bundled and persisted plugin registries and channel/provider sidecars were disabled only to bound source-startup cost. Layer parsing, composition, Gateway activation, RPC reads, and persistence guards remained active.

## Scope and non-goals

Included:

- ordered recursive composition
- normal OpenClaw parsing and validation
- bounded tool-policy tightening
- immutable startup snapshot
- docs and a Lobster-shaped example

Not included:

- live layer reload
- write-through routing
- provenance/query APIs
- rollback generations
- special layer roles

## Maintainer decision

This remains a draft because the product decision is explicit: should OpenClaw support ordered, immutable startup layers as a core Gateway contract, or require hosts to flatten configuration externally? The implementation and evidence now cover the bounded V1 either way.

Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34
